utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This the case number IT-99-37-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Milutinovic, Nikola Sainovic, Dragoljub Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And may we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: For the Prosecution, Geoffrey Nice, Cristina Romano, Milbert Shin, and our case manager, Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nice. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Eugene O'Sullivan, appearing on behalf of Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, Vladimir Petrovic, appearing as Defence counsel for Mr. Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Tomislav Visnjic for Dragoljub Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have a number of matters to get through in this conference. Is there a problem with the translation? Is it working now? We'll continue then. So we have a number of matters to deal with in this Status Conference and I will proceed immediately, and call on the parties as appropriate. First, as to pending motions. We have the Ojdanic application for binding orders addressed to certain NATO states. We are awaiting submissions from four states. I'm aware that we have received a reply from one, and we're waiting a reply from the others. Then there are two matters pending before the Appeals Chamber, one relating to the Ojdanic motion for additional funds and the other to the motion challenging jurisdiction over events in Kosovo. There is also a Prosecution application relating to disclosure of witness statements. And I have to say that the Chamber will be dealing with that as soon as possible. Just to remind ourselves, the instructions given were that the Prosecution was to file its pre-trial brief no later than one month after the Appeals Chamber decision on the preliminary motion and Defence pre-trial briefs to be filed three months later. I turn now to pre-trial preparation and disclosure of witness statements under 66(A)(i) are completed for all three accused and 66(A)(ii) statements disclosure to all three accused completed, with the exception of two remaining witnesses in respect of whom an application was made for an extension of protective measures. Mr. Nice, can you say anything about the -- the progress in relation to contacting these witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I can, but I'll see if one of my colleagues can assist on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry I'm not able to provide an immediate answer to this. Just give me one second and I'll be able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let me go on, Mr. Nice, and we'll come back to it. Yes. I turn next to expert witnesses. All expert reports have been disclosed both in B/C/S and English. There is, I understand, one potential issue, and it relates to the report of Patrick Ball. The Ojdanic Defence, I understand, would like to have the underlying material used in respect of that report and the Prosecution takes the position that this is not required unless it forms part of the actual report. But I understand the Ojdanic Defence should be in a position to bring us up to date on that. Mr. Visnjic, could you let us know where we stand on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we haven't made much headway with regard to this particular issue for a simple reason: In our contacts with the Prosecution, we received a request of theirs to deal with this material more precisely, so to speak, and to provide them with lists. We have reduced the material involved, in view of the pending ruling of the Appeals Chamber. We have stopped working on this particular matter. We are waiting for the ruling of the Appeals Chamber, and then we are going to continue our contacts with the Prosecution with regard to that particular matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: A ruling of the Appeals Chamber on which matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Funds, Your Honour. Funds for the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. I see. Very well. Well, at some stage you may want to consider whether you wish to put in a motion for the Chamber's consideration on that matter. And you may sit down, Mr. Visnjic. I understand, Mr. Nice, that the Prosecution is considering adding another constitutional law expert in light of what happened in the Milosevic case in relation to the evidence of Ivan Kristan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, that's in development. I may by now -- I may have identified another suitable expert and approaches may be made within days. But knowing how long this material takes to -- well, knowing how long it takes to find a willing expert and then how long it takes to prepare the report, I'd prefer not to be bound by any time limit at the moment and prefer to report back at the next Status Conference on that, if that's acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's also relevant for the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's relevant for the Milosevic case, and the time limit of that is rather tighter, as Your Honour knows. I'm very anxious to, at the least, be able to serve a report before we run out of time in the Milosevic case so that the material may be available; but I'm doing the best I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I should have been able to tell you and can now the two witnesses to whom you refer are apparently dealt with compendiously in the recent filing. We have no further information to provide at the moment beyond that in the filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Rule 68 disclosure, the instructions given at the last conference was that the Prosecution should disclose 68 material by the time their pre-trial brief is to be filed. That itself is one month after the Appeals Chamber decision on the preliminary motion. And the Prosecution was to report whether there was 68 material for which the consent of the provider has not yet been provided pursuant to Rule 70. Mr. Nice, are you in a position to say whether consent has been given in respect of the relevant material?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to say that it's been obtained --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please. Microphone for Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to say it's been obtained in respect of every item of such material yet. Where the consent has not yet been obtained, we are actively pursuing it. In the event of any irreconcilable conflicts between the Rules, we will -- that seem incapable of resolution, we will notify the Chamber immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And since you're on your feet, on 68 material in general, where are you in relation to the disclosure of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I can give a quantitative answer to that. As the Chamber will know, we've pursued the policy in this case, as in another case, of identifying the search criteria and pressing ahead with the searches in an orderly way and as rapidly as we can. Notwithstanding the suspension of proceedings following the Appeal Chamber's decision, we've continued to be turning over Rule 68 material in an orderly way and as soon as we reasonably can. It seems to us that meets the Rule 68 requirement -- duty that falls upon us, and there's the fourth report that has been filed and I think Ms. Romano may be in a position to speak about that, but it's all dealt within that report at the moment. The report deals with the position up until the date of the report, and I think also it gives lists of material filed from the beginning of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn next to reciprocal disclosure. And the Ojdanic Defence had invoked the reciprocal disclosure regime, and my understanding is that the issues relating to that have been resolved. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. It was only yesterday that we exchanged with the Prosecution a number of documents that we had received from the National Committee of Yugoslavia for Cooperation with The Hague Tribunal. We have a total of eight requests there. Only our first request has been dealt with so far, and that's the one we submitted in October 2002. And I hope that this pace will accelerate, because otherwise we are going to have problems in the future. If some other issues are not resolved, we are going to file additional requests to them, depending on how the investigation proceeds. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the topic of reciprocal disclosure, may I simply recall the following, so that it's on the record: In light of the disclosure regime existing with the Ojdanic Defence, we provided them with material that, in the event, was a provision in excess of what a Rule 70 provider had authorised. Once we discovered this, we drew it to the attention of the Ojdanic team. They were good enough to agree to return the material, which had been delivered to them, in order that the terms of the Rule 70 provider could be adhered to. And I'm grateful for the fact that they're providing that material back to us or returning it to us, and I understand that those -- that material and all copies of it will be back to us soon. The conditions upon which the material was to be made available to the Ojdanic team are being complied with forthwith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And I'd like to commend the Ojdanic Defence team for their fraternal and cooperative spirit. I turn next to the question of agreed facts. The Prosecutor had proposed to the Defence the three accused persons to seek agreement on facts on the basis of the indictment on a statement-by-statement basis. Now, that has been done in relation to the accused Milutinovic and the accused Ojdanic, but the Sainovic Defence team proposed a different methodology, that is, a list of facts which would go beyond the statement-by-statement approach in relation to the indictment. I have to say that the Chamber has considered this matter and the Chamber finds that the approach proposed by the Sainovic Defence team is a reasonable one and that it should be followed in relation to Sainovic. Mr. Petrovic, you should first start the ball rolling by proposing a list of agreed facts to the -- to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for this decision and thank you for your understanding of the approach that we had opted for in this matter. On behalf of Mr. Sainovic's Defence, I can say that we are going to prepare a set of facts as early as possible that we consider to be convenient for being dealt with by way of facts that are not in dispute, agreed facts. So I hope that we will proceed this way as you suggested. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And proceed as expeditiously as possible. And I want to clarify: This is, of course, without prejudice to the agreement that has already been reached by the Prosecutor and the other accused. Rule 92 bis, I'm told that instructions have been given for the parties to consider the best possible use of Rule 92 bis and to start discussions on this once the Prosecution witness list has been served. In the circumstances of the case, I say no more about that at this stage. I turn now to the length of the trial and the witnesses. Mr. Nice, at an earlier stage an indication had been given by the Prosecutor, an estimate of 100 to 120 witnesses. And for the Prosecution's case in chief to last approximately three to four months. Would you like to update me on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think this is an estimate. The earlier figures can stand, but of course we have yet to reach the stage where the 65 ter list is finally submitted, and we have no knowledge at the moment of what may be the time benefits of 92 bis agreements or rulings, and so the estimate stands but things may, inevitably, change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask if there is any issue which any of the parties would wish to raise now. Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's nothing we want to raise. We may, of course, have matters to which we want to respond. There may be matters to which we would like to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There's nothing for today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I just would briefly like to take the opportunity to comment on the status of the case from the perspective of the Ojdanic Defence team. And as far as we're concerned, the status of the case as it stands today is very poor, because we have not been working for the last six months and not been able to prepare for the trial. General Ojdanic deserves to have a strong preparation and a strong defence so that he has a fair trial. And the Prosecution has in the meantime had the resources to continue working during all that time and we believe that it's a very unfortunate situation, and I don't think that we could let the Status Conference pass without calling that to the attention of the Pre-Trial Judge. We hope that when we see you in the next four months or so, that the circumstances will be more favourable and more equitable at that time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I know the matter that you're referring to, and it's not really within the -- the competence of the Trial Chamber. But my understanding is that the matter is being dealt with at expeditiously as possible by the Appeals Chamber, and a ruling should be given in a relatively short time. May I then turn to the accused persons and inquire whether there's any matter that they wish to raise concerning their conditions of detention or any other matter relating to the -- to the case. I start with Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MILUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, nothing for this moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milutinovic. Mr. Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED SAINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Nothing at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ojdanic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED OJDANIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, nothing to raise at this moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ojdanic. The next conference must be held on or before the -- Thursday, the 22nd of January. And I'm fixing Wednesday, the 21st of January as the date for the next -- the next conference. Is there any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not. The hearing stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.58 p.m.
